executive_summary: MRR reached $421,512 in 2025-12 (+5.04% MoM, ARR $5,058,144) across 1,244 active customers, but growth is acquisition-led: trailing-12-month NRR averages 99.3%, so expansion ($82,097 TTM) does not fully replace churned MRR ($98,662 TTM). Logo churn averaging 4.2% a month is the main drag on compounding. Unit economics split sharply by channel: Referral (5.27x LTV:CAC), Organic Search (4.95x) and Content/SEO (4.17x) clear the 3x benchmark, while Paid Social (2.51x), Paid Search (2.11x) and Outbound Sales (1.99x) do not and take 10.1 to 13.6 months to pay back.

key_risks.title: Net revenue retention is below 100%
key_risks.evidence: Average TTM NRR is 99.3% (99.6% in the latest month); TTM expansion MRR is $82,097 against $98,662 of churned MRR.
key_risks.so_what: Revenue growth depends on new-logo acquisition (TTM new MRR $267,906). Any slowdown in acquisition spend shows up directly as flat or falling MRR.

key_risks.title: Three channels sit below the 3x LTV:CAC benchmark
key_risks.evidence: Paid Search 2.11x (CAC $4,385, 12.8-month payback), Outbound Sales 1.99x (CAC $4,582, 13.6 months), Paid Social 2.51x (CAC $3,045, 10.1 months). They also carry the largest spend: $1,512,963, $1,026,464 and $995,570.
key_risks.so_what: The most capital-intensive channels return the least per dollar; payback beyond 12 months strains cash if churn stays elevated.

key_risks.title: Most expected churn loss sits outside the 'high-risk' list
key_risks.evidence: Expected 3-month MRR loss is $6,439 in the high tier, $9,076 in the medium tier and $18,238 in the low tier, of $33,752 in total. The top three MRR deciles hold 72.2% of MRR; Enterprise North America (22.5%) and Europe (22.4%) are the largest segments.
key_risks.so_what: A playbook aimed only at the top-risk accounts covers a minority of expected loss. Large Enterprise accounts need protection regardless of score because of concentration.

opportunities.title: Re-weight acquisition toward low-CAC channels
opportunities.evidence: Referral delivers 5.27x LTV:CAC at a CAC of $1,658 with a 5.5-month payback; Organic Search 4.95x at $1,819.
opportunities.so_what: Shifting incremental budget here improves payback fastest. Marginal returns may fall as these channels scale; that is not measurable from this data.

opportunities.title: Engagement-triggered retention outreach
opportunities.evidence: The selected Logistic Regression model reaches ROC-AUC 0.691 with a top-decile lift of 2.57x (precision 0.283 vs a 0.1102 baseline). Engagement score is the strongest driver. 125 customers ($24,692 MRR) are high-risk and 248 ($61,739 MRR) medium-risk.
opportunities.so_what: A usable early-warning signal exists a quarter ahead of churn, enough to prioritise customer-success time.

opportunities.title: Upgrade path from Growth to Enterprise
opportunities.evidence: Growth in North America has 167 customers at an ARPA of $215.9, versus $818.9 ARPA for Enterprise in the same region.
opportunities.so_what: Expansion is the lever that lifts NRR above 100%; the existing Growth base is the nearest pool of upgrade candidates.

recommended_actions.action: Launch an engagement-drop playbook (health review, exec check-in, usage coaching) for the 125 high-risk and 248 medium-risk accounts.
recommended_actions.success_metric: Realised 3-month churn in the contacted high-risk group below the 11.02% baseline, measured against a holdout.
recommended_actions.rationale: Largest controllable revenue leak; model signal is moderate but actionable.

recommended_actions.action: Cap further spend growth in Paid Search, Outbound Sales and Paid Social until CAC payback is back under 12 months; pilot added budget in Referral and Content/SEO.
recommended_actions.success_metric: Channel LTV:CAC at or above 3x and payback under 12 months.
recommended_actions.rationale: These three channels fall below the benchmark while absorbing most of the spend.

recommended_actions.action: Assign executive sponsors to the largest Enterprise accounts in North America and Europe regardless of churn score.
recommended_actions.success_metric: Zero unplanned Enterprise logo losses; track Enterprise gross retention monthly.
recommended_actions.rationale: Segment concentration (22.5% and 22.4% of MRR) makes single-account loss material.

recommended_actions.action: Build a Growth-to-Enterprise upgrade campaign starting with the North America Growth base.
recommended_actions.success_metric: NRR above 100% for three consecutive months.
recommended_actions.rationale: Pushes NRR above the 99.3% TTM average through expansion rather than acquisition.

recommended_actions.action: Refresh the forecast monthly and track it against its backtest error before using it in planning.
recommended_actions.success_metric: Realised error within the 2.86% 6-month backtest MAPE.
recommended_actions.rationale: The band is estimated from only 6 backtest origins and is likely optimistic.

caveats: The dataset is synthetic (1,800 customers, 24 months); figures demonstrate the method, not a real business.
The churn model is moderate (ROC-AUC 0.691): use it to prioritise outreach, not to predict individual accounts. Engagement is associated with churn here, but the effect of intervening is untested.
The forecast ($570,878 in six months, band $551,069 to $590,688) is a damped trend, not a pipeline-based plan, and its band comes from only 6 backtest origins.
